title: Unramified diagonal yields an etale scheme atlas
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $S$. Its relative diagonal $\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$ is unramified if and only if there exists a scheme $W$ and a representable surjective etale morphism $W\to\mathcal X$. Thus this condition is equivalent to being a Deligne--Mumford stack in the scheme-atlas convention of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Etale means [def-weil-etale-morphism], tested on scheme charts. An algebraic stack here is a stack in groupoids on schemes with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stacks, representability and scheme atlases use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and smooth means [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Open substacks are full substacks whose pullback by every scheme is an open subscheme. A representable morphism is unramified if every scheme base change, on etale scheme charts of its algebraic-space source, is unramified in [def-weil-unramified-morphism].

source.place: Tag 06N3 (theorem-DM), equivalence (1)--(3); relative-base convention via Tag 050N (lemma-separated-implies-morphism-separated), part (1).

proof.text: First note that a map $H\to\mathcal X$ from a scheme is representable by algebraic spaces: for a scheme $T\to\mathcal X$, the groupoid $H\times_{\mathcal X}T$ is the base change of the representable diagonal along $H\times_ST\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$. Its objects are triples $(h,t,\alpha)$ with $\alpha$ an isomorphism in $\mathcal X$; its automorphisms fixing $h,t$ are identities. Thus it is an algebraic space, by the definition of a representable diagonal. We use these triple descriptions for all fibre-product identifications below.

Suppose $q:W\to\mathcal X$ is a surjective etale scheme atlas. Set $R=W\times_{\mathcal X}W$. Its first projection $p_1:R\to W$ is etale by base change. Hence $p_1$ is unramified. The map $j=(p_1,p_2):R\to W\times_SW$ is unramified by cancellation applied to $R\xrightarrow{j}W\times_SW\xrightarrow{\mathrm{pr}_1}W$. The morphism $W\times_SW\to\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X$ is the composite of two base changes of $q$, so is surjective, flat and locally finitely presented. The base change of $\Delta_{\mathcal X/S}$ by this cover is exactly $j$. Descent of unramifiedness therefore proves that the relative diagonal is unramified.

source.place: Tag 06N3 (theorem-DM), (3) implies (1), via lemma-properties-covering-imply-diagonal; the same proof over S.

proof.text: Conversely assume $\Delta_{\mathcal X/S}$ unramified, and fix a finite-type point $x$. Choose $a:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathcal X$ representing it as in the field-representative lemma; $a$ is locally of finite type and $R_a=\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Spec}k$ has etale projections. Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal X$. Set $F=U\times_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Spec}k$. Then $F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth and surjective by base change, so $F$ is nonempty, and $F\to U$ is locally of finite type as a base change of $a$.

source.place: Tag 06N3 (theorem-DM), first construction paragraph and the first fibre square.

proof.text: The triple description gives $F\times_UF\cong R_a\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}F$, using one projection $R_a\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ for the fibre product and the other for its second map to $F$. In particular both projections $F\times_UF\to F$ are etale. The diagonal $F\to F\times_UF$ is a morphism over $F$ between two spaces etale over $F$ (the identity of $F$ and the first projection), so it is etale. It is a monomorphism: a pair of arrows from a test scheme agreeing after this diagonal already agree after either projection. The etale-monomorphism lemma makes it an open immersion. Since $F\to U$ is locally of finite type, the open-diagonal criterion proves that $F\to U$ is unramified.

source.place: Tag 06N3 (theorem-DM), paragraph containing F times_U F and Delta_(F/U).

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine scheme $V$ etale over $F$, by taking a nonempty affine open in an etale scheme cover of the nonempty algebraic space $F$. Then $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth by composition, while $b:V\to U$ is unramified by composition of the etale, hence unramified, $V\to F$ with $F\to U$. The dense-separable-points lemma supplies a closed point $v\in V$ with $\kappa(v)/k$ finite separable. Let $u=b(v)$.

source.place: Tag 06N3 (theorem-DM), choice of nonempty affine V and separable closed point v; Varieties 056U.

proof.text: Write $A=\mathcal O_{U,u}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{V,v}$. Smoothness is affine-locally smoothness of k-algebras, so the smooth-over-field regularity lemma makes $B$ regular local. The unramified local criterion gives $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$. The images of elements of $\mathfrak m_A$ therefore span $\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak m_B^2$ over $\kappa(v)$; choose finitely many of them forming a basis. Nakayama for the finitely generated $B$-module $\mathfrak m_B$ shows that these images minimally generate $\mathfrak m_B$. The regular-local-generators lemma makes this list a regular sequence. Represent the chosen germs in $A$ by sections $f_1,\ldots,f_d$ on a common open neighbourhood $U_0$ of $u$. Each vanishes at $u$, and their pullbacks to $B$ generate $\mathfrak m_B$ and form a regular sequence. Empty lists are allowed if $B$ is a field.

The map $U_0\to\mathcal X$ is smooth, hence flat and locally finitely presented. Its field fibre is the open subspace $F_0=U_0\times_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Spec}k=F\times_UU_0$ of $F$, and $V_0=b^{-1}(U_0)=V\times_FF_0$ is an etale scheme chart $V_0\to F_0$ by base change, containing $v$ with $\mathcal O_{V_0,v}=B$. Apply the fibrewise regular-slice lemma to these functions and the point $v$. After shrinking $U_0$ around $u$, their zero scheme $Z=V(f_1,\ldots,f_d)\subset U_0$ is flat and locally of finite presentation over $\mathcal X$. All shrinks contain $u$ and hence preserve $v$ and its local ring; since the functions vanish at $u$, this point belongs to $Z$.

Replace $V_0$ by $b^{-1}(U_0)$ for the shrunken $U_0$, still an etale chart of the field fibre containing $v$, and $T=Z\times_{U_0}V_0$. This is exactly the zero scheme in $V_0$ cut out by the pulled-back functions, so $\mathcal O_{T,v}=B/(f_1,\ldots,f_d)B=B/\mathfrak m_B=\kappa(v)$. The map $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type: affine-locally $V_0$ is a smooth finite-type k-algebra and $T$ is its quotient by the indicated equations. For its local map at $v$, the ideal generated by the maximal ideal of k is zero, the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{T,v}$ is also zero, and the residue extension is the finite separable $\kappa(v)/k$. The unramified local criterion therefore gives an open neighbourhood of $v$ in $T$ unramified over k.

source.place: Tag 06N3 (theorem-DM), local ring of the zero scheme T and application of Morphisms 02GF.

proof.text: The cartesian identities give an etale chart $T=Z\times_{U_0}V_0\to Z\times_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Spec}k$. Indeed it is the base change of $V_0\to F_0$, and its defining equations are exactly the pullbacks already used to define $T$. At $v$, $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is unramified by the preceding local-ring calculation. Apply the fibrewise etale-locus lemma to the flat locally finitely presented $Z\to\mathcal X$ and this chart. An open neighbourhood $W_x\subset Z$ of $u$ maps etale to $\mathcal X$. The retained point $v$ in its field fibre proves that the image of $W_x$ contains $x$.

source.place: Tag 06N3 (theorem-DM), zero scheme T and application of Tag 06N2 (lemma-etale-at-point).

proof.text: Do this for each finite-type point $x$, choosing one $W_x$ for each. Use one fixed smooth atlas $U$ in all the constructions, so each $W_x$ is an open subscheme of a closed subscheme of an open of $U$. The point classes form a set (a quotient of the points of $U$); this indexing set and these locally closed subschemes have a common bound in the universe containing $U$. Hence their coproduct belongs to that universe. Form $W=\coprod_xW_x$. The stack descent condition glues the objects on the disjoint open cover of $W$ into $q:W\to\mathcal X$, whose restrictions are the maps just constructed. Chartwise source locality makes $q$ representable etale, hence flat and locally finitely presented. Its image contains every finite-type point. The finite-type-point detection lemma now proves that $q$ is surjective. This also covers the empty stack: the family and $W$ are empty and the detection lemma still applies.

source.place: Tag 06N3 (theorem-DM), final disjoint-union and finite-type-point argument.

proof.text: Both implications are proved. In the fixed convention a Deligne--Mumford stack is precisely a stack with representable diagonal and a surjective etale scheme atlas. The representable diagonal and the stack condition were already assumed, and maps from schemes are representable by step 1. Thus the asserted equivalence with the Deligne--Mumford terminology is exactly this definition.

Proof: the 11 steps follow 06N3. (3)=>(1) is proved by cancellation (pr1 composed with j equals p1) and 04XD descent along W x_S W -> X x_S X, whose pullback of the diagonal is R. For (1)=>(3), the field representative's étale self-relation gives F x_U F = R_a x_k F. Its diagonal is étale by the 03FV clause and is a monomorphism, hence an open immersion by 05W5, so F->U is unramified by 05W1(2). A separable closed point v (056U), a regular B (00TT), m_A B = m_B (02GF), Nakayama (00DV) and 00NQ give d = dim B regular parameters. Then come the 06MD slice, O_{T,v} = kappa(v) with unramified near v by 02GF, the étale chart T -> Z x_X k (cartesian identity checked) and the 06N2 étale locus. The coproduct glues by étale descent, and 06G2/04XL/04XI detection gives surjectivity, the empty stack included. Step 11 is the DM definition of def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids.
